title: What is Baltimore best at making? 'Criminals,' says Marlon Humphrey who then feels the heat and changes tune
text:
The Ravens defensive back faced social media backlash for the comment about the city where he's played since 2017

'Heinous' crime sparks major concerns over blue city: 'What is happening there?!'

Violent crime rates fuel debate on 'Outnumbered' as panelists react to recent high-profile killings in Chicago, Philadelphia and New York City. The co-hosts criticize progressive prosecutors and bail reform policies for releasing dangerous individuals, pointing to three tragic homicide cases.

Marlon Humphrey is sorry. No, really. He took a jab at the city of Baltimore and its crime rate this week and had to quickly walk that back with an apology on Wednesday.

The Baltimore Ravens defensive back in his latest Marlon Humphrey podcast took on the question of what Baltimore is best at making?

So... crab cakes?

Old Bay Seasoning?

Nope.

"They're best at making criminals," Humphrey said.

Lordy!

Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey revealed that meeting President Trump at an event left quite an impression on him. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)

SHOOTING NEAR BALTIMORE YOUTH FOOTBALL EVENT LEAVES 12-YEAR-OLD GIRL DEAD, 3 ADULTS WOUNDED

Humphrey chuckled after his comment but, as Scripture says, out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

The comment about the town where Humphrey has played since 2017 was predictably rebuked in the media and on social media. And that led Humphrey to face questions about his comment in the Ravens' locker room on Wednesday.

RAVENS PLAYERS RIDE WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP IN MOTORCADE, GET SHOUTOUT DURING SPEECH AT BALTIMORE SHIPYARD EVENT

Apology incoming, folks.

"As you guys know, I've been there my whole career," Humphrey told reporters. "Spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here, and I'm an investor in the city, investor different areas and parts of the state.

"But obviously, I do know the effect that words have, so I'd just like to apologize for those comments."

President Donald Trump speaks with Baltimore Ravens player Marlon Humphrey as Ryan Eckley and Nick Moore look on upon arrival in Sparrows Point, Md., on Oct. 6, 2026, ahead of an event at Anduril Industries. (AFP via Getty Images)

This is Humphrey apologizing for articulating a thought born of an inconvenient truth.

FBI REPORTS LARGEST DROP IN VIOLENT CRIME AND MURDER SINCE 1937 AS HOMICIDES FALL MORE THAN 18%

Baltimore’s crime rates are historically higher than the national average and rank it among the higher-crime large metropolitan areas in the United States.

Analyses from various public safety trackers consistently place Baltimore among the leaders per capita for both violent and property crime, outpacing the vast majority of U.S. cities.

FBI REPORTS 114% JUMP IN VIOLENT CRIME ARRESTS UNDER TRUMP COMPARED TO BIDEN’S FINAL MONTHS

The statistics:

Violent Crime Rate: Baltimore’s violent crime rate historically hovers around 1,500 to 1,600+ incidents per 100,000 residents, compared to a national average that is typically under 400 per 100,000.

Homicide Trends: For years, Baltimore struggled with stubbornly high homicide numbers, recording upwards of 300 murders annually between 2015 and 2022. However, the city has experienced a sharp, multi-year decline. Homicides dropped significantly to roughly 200 in 2024 and have continued a downward trajectory.

Property Crime and Motor Vehicle Theft: Property crime—including larceny-theft, burglary, and motor vehicle theft—makes up the bulk of offenses in the city. Auto thefts have historically been a prominent issue; data analysis indicates that residents face a noticeably higher-than-average statistical risk of vehicle theft compared to the broader national scope.

Those are the stats. The factoids.

But it is understandable the people of Baltimore heard a player who has said and done some controversial or unpopular things, depending on one's political beliefs, and simply could not agree with statistics or Humphrey's opinion.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Baltimore residents spent the past few hours rallying to the side of their town and it started on social media.

That left Humphrey trying to reply to the criticism.

"I love this city," he said. "I think I've expressed this many times."

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.
